$comment: NEW-55 (voice V4, phase-2 plan approved 2026-10-27 on #NEW-9): CALLER MODE. A call = a conversation with ONE agent by voice: the microphone stays open until End call, every finished utterance goes out as a plain message through `sessions.send` (the member's conversation with that agent, exactly like push to talk), every reply of that agent in that conversation is spoken, speech while a reply plays cancels it (barge-in), and an utterance finished while the agent's turn runs rides the existing queue bar (the `queue` slot strip) like a typed message. Recognition and the voice run ONLY on the member's voice device (`user_voice_settings.voiceDeviceId`); phones (V5) and web (V6) STREAM the call's audio to it. ENTRY: the telephone (icon concept `voice-call`, testId `testIds.call`, label `copy.call`) in the AGENT CHAT'S HEADER ×4, left of the overflow, the existing header icon button; never in the Agents list. The IDE tray's `Call {agent}` item (voice.json `trayCall`) calls the voice agent. AVAILABILITY = pure `callAvailability(input)` (`availabilityCases`; reasons in order, first match wins): no voice device → `noVoiceDevice`; Speak replies off → `speakOff` (the voice is only prepared while it is on); the voice device offline → `offline`; on a desktop that is NOT the voice device → `notHere` (V4 calls only from the voice device's own IDE); the voice device's doctor row `speech` (group voice) missing or not yet checked → `preparing`; its state `missing` (no usable GPU: Qwen3-TTS runs on the GPU only) → `noGpu`; a call already running on the voice device → `busy`; else enabled (reason null). A disabled telephone stays visible, dimmed, its tooltip/long-press = the reason. FLOW = pure `callStep(state, event)` + `callView(state)` (`flowCases`; the SAME machine on the voice device and on a caller, which receives the host's events as `call_event` frames): phases connecting → listening ⇄ thinking ⇄ speaking, `muted` is a flag (the microphone closes, replies still play); `view` null = no call surface. The call surface: on the desktop THE voice capsule (voice-call-overlay: VoiceWave md, `state` bold, `line` muted, then the `mute` pill and the PRIMARY `copy.endCall` pill), on phones full screen and on web a centred card (the `voice-call` entry: VoiceWave xl, the state, the line, End call primary + Mute); a failure ends the call with a toast (`toast`): `copy.failed` by code, the relay's `busy` included; a web browser without WebCodecs Opus keeps the telephone enabled (availability never asks) and a press toasts `unsupported` without dialing (#NEW-70: Opus only, no PCM wire kind). `surfaceSpecimens` are the styleguide rows of both surfaces (web + desktop `voice-call-overlay` capsules with the lead pill, and the `voice-call` entry); each view's End call pill is `copy.endCall`. TRANSPORT (streamed calls): tRPC `voice.startCall({agentId})` answers `{callId, ticket, url, relayUrl}` (the client dials `url` as-is) or refuses with the availability reason; the caller opens the steer relay with a `caller` ticket (claims callId, deviceId, deviceOwnerId); the relay rings the voice device on its control socket (`{t:'call_ring', callId, agentId}`), which mints a `call_host` ticket (tRPC `voice.callHostTicket({callId})`) and joins; both get `{t:'call_ready'}`; no host within `constants.ringTimeoutMs` → the caller gets `{t:'error', code:'no_answer'}` then `bye`. The `call_host` ticket names the voice device (`deviceId`) and is admitted only into that device's room. Once paired, each socket may send at most `constants.maxFramesPerSecond` binary frames per second (a token bucket; extra frames are dropped), a call ends after `constants.maxCallMs` (reason `max_length`) and after `constants.idleTimeoutMs` without a frame either way (reason `idle`): both sides get `call_end` with that reason. A `call_end` reaches the flow as `hungUp {reason?}` (`hangUpRules`): a reason (`idle`, `max_length`, or `dropped` when the other socket went away) fails the call as `dropped` with its toast; ONLY a reason-less hang-up (the other side pressed End call) ends silently. Mute never stops the frames: a muted caller keeps sending silence (web its disabled track's, the phones ENCODED SILENCE, one `up` frame per `constants.frameMs`), so muting never trips `idle`. BACKGROUND: a phone call KEEPS RUNNING with the screen locked or another app in front (iOS the `audio` background mode with AVAudioSession playAndRecord / voiceChat, Android the `microphone` foreground service with its ongoing `Call {agent}` notification); only End call or the far side ends it, and while the call surface shows the screen never dims on its own. Another call taking the audio (an incoming phone call: iOS an AVAudioSession interruption that began, Android audio focus LOSS or LOSS_TRANSIENT, or focus refused at start) fails the call as `dropped`; signing out or switching accounts ends it. DEPLOY ORDER: the steer relay ships BEFORE web (an older relay refuses caller tickets with 401, which also count toward its failed-auth rate limit). The voice device answers every ring without asking: a caller is always the device's own member. AUDIO = BINARY WebSocket frames: byte 0 = kind (`wire.kinds`), bytes 1-2 = sequence (u16 big-endian, wraps), then ONE Opus packet of `constants.frameMs` ms; uplink mono `constants.upRate` Hz at ~`constants.upKbps` kbps (web and the voice device's encoder add in-band FEC; the phones' platform encoders expose no FEC switch and send none), downlink mono `constants.downRate` Hz at ~`constants.downKbps` kbps; a frame above `wire.maxFrameBytes` is dropped; a caller may send only `up`, the host only `down`. CONTROL = JSON text frames `wire.control`; the relay forwards them between the pair, persists nothing and never decodes audio. The caller plays the downlink through a `constants.jitterMs` ms jitter buffer, flushed on `call_event` speechStarted (barge-in), and captures with the OS echo canceller on (iOS `.voiceChat`, Android VOICE_COMMUNICATION + AcousticEchoCanceler, web `echoCancellation: true`); the voice device's own microphone runs through the worker's echo canceller with the reply as the reference. In a call the worker closes a segment after `constants.minSilenceMs` ms of silence (push to talk keeps talk-listen.json's 300) and barge-in needs `constants.bargeInMs` ms of speech.

reasons.noVoiceDevice: Pick a voice device in Settings → Voice
reasons.speakOff: Turn on Speak replies in Settings → Voice

control.call_ring: relay → voice device (control socket): { callId, agentId }
control.call_ready: relay → both: the pair is up
control.call_event: host → caller: { event } = one `flowCases` event (partial, said, queued, replyStarted, replyFinished, speechStarted)
control.call_end: either → relay → the other: { reason? }; the relay then closes the room; the receiver steps `hungUp {reason}`
